correctness.rationale: From \(A+B=C\) and \(A^2=B^2=0\), the identity \(CA+AC=C^2\) forces all blocks except opposite nonzero eigenpairs and the zero eigenblock. Selfadjointness makes each paired block an anti-isometry torsor, possible precisely under the finite-field determinant-class test. The zero block is parametrized by isotropic image \(r\)-planes and invertible symmetric maps \(U^*\to U\). Isotropic-line and orthogonal-group order formulas produce every coefficient. The ten fixed exact field cases and all 258 ternary diagonal tests matched by direct matrix arithmetic; finite verification is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result addresses the natural multiplicity refinement of the known classification problem, determining exactly how many pairs of square-zero selfadjoint summands realize each split-semisimple target at each rank. It is uniform over all odd finite fields, all dimensions and all Witt types, and exhibits a determinant obstruction plus a full Witt-index-controlled interval of ranks. The precise invariant is useful for constrained matrix-decomposition distributions and classical-group orbit counts; no stronger downstream theorem is presumed.
